statements.text: In an era when artificial intelligence technology is rapidly advancing, election administrators would benefit from comprehensive guidance in order to effectively counter potential threats to our election processes.
statements.venue: Press release on Preparing Election Administrators for AI Act

statements.text: Using AI, it is remarkably easy to imitate voices or send out a video where someone who is running for office appears to be doing something or saying something that is utterly fake.
statements.venue: NBC News, comments on the fake Biden robocall

statements.text: This unanimous decision from the FCC will help protect Americans from scammers who are using artificial intelligence to try to trick them into giving up their personal information and hard-earned money. This ruling is a positive step forward. Congress has a responsibility to carefully consider and address the challenges associated with artificial intelligence.
statements.venue: Press release on FCC ruling on AI robocalls

statements.text: This unanimous decision from the EAC will help protect Americans from scammers who are using artificial intelligence to attempt to corrupt our electoral processes. Congress has a responsibility to carefully consider and address the challenges associated with artificial intelligence. That is why I am continuing to support the Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act.
statements.venue: Press release on Election Assistance Commission vote

statements.text: Why isn't the answer to watermark posts to indicate not whether they are AI generated, but rather where they originate?
statements.context: Senate hearing on foreign threats to the 2024 U.S. elections, questioning a technology provider about content provenance.

statements.text: In a rapidly evolving digital landscape, we must ensure that voters are not manipulated by purposely misleading AI-generated content. This bill is a necessary step to strengthen the integrity of our elections while also protecting First Amendment rights.
statements.venue: Press release on Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act

statements.text:
I was honored to receive the National Conference of State Legislatures' 2025 Restoring the Balance Award for my work opposing a federal moratorium on state artificial intelligence laws.

As AI and related technologies continue to evolve rapidly, state lawmakers must retain the ability to set their own policies in response to new developments.

I’m grateful to the @NCSLorg for this recognition and for its continued work to defend the critical role of state lawmakers.
The adoption of these technologies, however, is not without risk. [...] It has the potential to introduce significant cyber risk if the AI systems themselves are not properly protected and managed.
statements.context: Senate Armed Services Committee open hearing on the nomination of Lt. Gen. Joshua Rudd to be Director of the NSA and Cyber Command.

statements.text: The best path forward will balance a recognition of AI’s promise — including breakthroughs in medical advances and accessibility — with its risks. Congress should work to protect our critical infrastructure and establish consumer protections, while also maintaining America’s leadership in AI innovation.

Maine families and small businesses are already paying some of the highest electricity costs in the nation. The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures that they will not pay an even steeper bill by directing state utility regulators to consider standards that would make high-volume users like AI data centers offset their own costs. Mainers should not have to pay the bill for data centers’ power generation, transmission lines, and energy infrastructure.
statements.venue: Statement on the Ratepayer Protection Act, via Newsweek

statements.text: I voted and cosponsored a bill that the Senate considered just last month to put guardrails and encourage states to adopt guardrails on the construction of data centers. That included making sure that they have no impact on electric rates, very important for a state like Maine with the fourth highest electric rates in the country due to Troy’s policies.
statements.venue: Maine Senate debate, as reported by Newsweek

statements.text: There may be a former mill site, as Governor [Janet] Mills has said, where a data center would work out all right because there is a source of power and water, but in many other places, they would not work well.
statements.venue: Maine Senate debate, as reported by Newsweek
